Opened 2026-08-09 ~7:20pm PDT. **Jake's spec, verbatim frame:** *"Take a rolling, trailing 3 month
S&P return and extrapolate it forward 3 months. If down buy a put so the breakeven is the extrapolated
number, same for a call if up. Straight line out 3 months as if that's where the S&P will be. If it is,
we break even. If it surpasses, make money. Roll forward a month at a time. Start at the beginning of
the dotcom boom."*

Tool: `tools/momentum_extrapolation_backtest_cell.py` (complete Colab cell; also ran in-session).
Chart: `raw/momentum-extrapolation-backtest-2026-08-09.png`.
Data: **SPX daily closes 1975→2026-08-07 from CBOE** (`SPX_History.csv`, primary source; last print
7757.64 matches FRED SP500 to the penny at the seam) · VIX from FRED VIXCLS (1990→) · DTB3 T-bill for
rates. Strike SOLVED per trade so breakeven = the extrapolated target exactly (Black-Scholes European,
1.8% flat dividend yield). **375 monthly trades, entries 1994-12-30 → 2026-05-01 (265 calls / 110 puts).**

**A property of Jake's construction, noted before the numbers (it makes the test unusually clean):**
pinning the breakeven AT the extrapolated target makes **hit rate ≡ P(the index lands beyond its own
trend line)** — identical under ANY volatility assumption (higher vol just moves the solved strike).
And per-trade $P&L = (S_expiry − target) in the trade's direction, floored at −premium. **The theory
(does the line get reached?) and the wrapper (what the bet costs) separate exactly.**

## DATA (computed — the run of 2026-08-09; reproduce with the cell)
**The theory's truth value (option-free):**
- **Hit rate all trades: 27.5%.** After UP 3-mo (calls): **31.7%**. After DOWN 3-mo (puts): **17.3%**.
- **Forward-vs-trailing regression: slope +0.022, corr +0.022** (n=375 overlapping monthly obs;
  overlap inflates significance — the point estimate is ~zero either way).
- **Mean gap (realized − extrapolated): +0.02pp overall; −3.72pp after up-trends; +9.03pp after
  down-trends** (declines mean-revert hard).

**What the option wrapper paid (mode A = VIX-priced):**
- ALL: mean RoP **−29.4%**, median **−100%**, **Σ −110.31× premiums** over 375 trades; **56.8% expired
  worthless**; avg premium 3.9% of spot.
- CALLS: mean −29.0%, Σ −76.8×. PUTS: mean −30.4%, Σ −33.5×, 60.9% wiped.
- **Mode B (realized-vol pricing = zero vol premium, a fantasy floor): calls flip POSITIVE (mean
  +31.3%, Σ +82.8×); puts still lose (−17.5%, Σ −19.3×).** The call-side sign lives entirely inside
  the volatility premium; the put-side loses even with free-vol pricing.
- VIX-multiplier sensitivity (Σ): ×0.85 → −55.3× · ×1.00 → −110.3× · ×1.15 → −136.6×.

**By era (mode A, Σ in premium units):** BOOM 95-00 **−17.9×** (hit 28.1%) · BUST 00-02 −5.1× (31.0%) ·
EXPANSION 02-07 −29.0× (21.7%) · **GFC 07-09 +17.7× (29.4%, the ONLY positive era)** · QE BULL 09-19
−45.9× (27.7%) · COVID 20-21 −9.6× (30.4%) · BEAR 2022 −2.3× (33.3%) · AI ERA 23-26 −18.2× (27.5%).

**Tails:** best trades **2008-09-02 put +1324%**, 2008-08-01 put +1127%, 2017-11-01 call +690%

**Caveats (directional):** flat-vol BS — real SPX put skew sits ABOVE VIX-flat, so **real puts are
MORE expensive than modeled → put results here are KINDER than reality**; OTM call IV sits below VIX →
call results slightly harsher than reality. No bid-ask/commissions (90s SPX spreads were wide).
Overlapping windows. Flat dividend yield.

## THESIS (interpretation — NOT fact)
- *(analysis — the headline)* **THE STRAIGHT LINE HAS NO FORECASTING CONTENT. Slope +0.02 means the
  trailing 3-month return tells you essentially NOTHING about the next 3 months** — the market lands
  beyond its own trend line ~1 time in 4, and you pay ~4% of spot per attempt to find out. The scatter
  panel is the whole result: the actual fit is a horizontal line; the extrapolation is a 45° line;
  the strategy is the gap between them, paid for in premium.
- *(analysis — ⭐ the anatomy is the finding)* **The construction survives in exactly one place —
  trailing +0..+5% (hit 52.5%, +17% mean, the only positive bucket) — and that is DRIFT WEARING A
  MOMENTUM COSTUME.** Extrapolating a small trend ≈ betting the market delivers its ordinary ~+2%/qtr
  drift, which it does about half the time. The signal is not the trend's direction; it is the trend's
  SIZE: the further trailing gets from drift, the deader the bet (>+10% trailing: 2.4% hit; <−10%:
  8.3%). **Extreme trends do not extend at slope — they revert.** *(Ties [[dip-buying-base-rates]]:
  same mean-reversion, opposite wrapper.)*
- *(analysis — the answer to the question as ASKED, "start at the dotcom boom")* **Even the greatest
  sustained rally in modern history lost 17.9× premiums to its own extrapolation.** The boom rose
  ~25%/yr — RELENTLESSLY but not ACCELERATINGLY. After a +10% quarter the spec demands ANOTHER +10%;
  the boom's steady-state was +5-6%. **A melt-up kills trend-acceleration bets by being steady.** The
  only era that paid was the GFC (+17.7×, carried by Aug/Sep-2008 puts at 11-13×): **the strategy is
  structurally a crash-convexity position that bleeds in every other regime — including the melt-ups
  it feels designed for.**
- *(analysis — the put side, and the vault's standing conclusion measured at 30-year scale)* Puts
  bought into declines needing FURTHER decline hit 17.3% and lose even at fantasy vol pricing,
  because the post-decline gap averages **+9pp of mean reversion** (the V-recovery). This is
  [[portfolio-state]] L827's *"90-day long options are structurally excluded"* and the L782 theta
  bill, now confirmed out-of-sample across three decades rather than derived from one book. *(⚠️
  scope: Jake's live SPY put is a HEDGE against a held book, not a momentum extrapolation — the L3471
  symmetry note stands; this backtest does NOT grade his position, it grades the trend-following
  wrapper.)*
- *(analysis — where the sign actually lives)* Mode B flipping calls to +31% mean says **the momentum
  theory's P&L is not about momentum: it is short the volatility risk premium.** Anyone selling you
  the option charges VIX-class vol; the underlying delivers less; the extrapolation bet pays that
  spread every month and collects only when a regime BREAKS (2008 legs, Jan-2018, the 2020 recovery
  — acceleration events, not trend events).
- *(discipline)* **This is the WARNING-vs-TRIGGER rule in backtest form: a trailing return is a STATE,
  and the spec converts a state into a timed, priced claim — which is exactly the conversion the rule
  bans, and the market charged −110× premiums for making it 375 times.** States shade odds; they do
  not time. The instrument now exists to test any future "the trend says" claim in one run.
